name: Apocarotenal
description: Apocarotenal (CAS 1107-26-2 ), also known as β-apo-8′-carotenal and listed as E160e in the EU, is a carotenoid-derived colorant used to deliver orange-to-red hues in food, supplement, and cosmetic formulations. It functions as both a pigment and an antioxidant stabilizer, offering formulators a natural-origin coloring option with dual functional value. In food manufacturing, E160e is used to color beverages and dairy products. It is also applied to margarine and processed foods where a warm orange tone is required within regulatory limits. Supplement and nutraceutical producers incorporate it into softgels and tablets for color standardization. The compound serves as a provitamin A source in these applications. In cosmetics, it is used to achieve natural-looking orange and peach tones in skin care and color cosmetics without synthetic azo dyes. Pharmaceutical coating applications also use it to tint tablet films and capsule shells to a consistent, recognizable color. Apocarotenal is supplied as a crystalline powder and in oil suspension or emulsified liquid forms. These formats are suited to both fat-soluble and water-dispersible formulations. Standard grades include food-grade and FCC -compliant specifications, with concentrations typically standardized at 10% in oil or emulsion formats. Bulk supply is available for industrial use, with smaller quantities offered for formulation development.
